perspectives.description: When a weakness is published against an algorithm, a protocol version, or a library, which of the deployed interfaces are affected — and, holding this record beside the one from last quarter, what has changed.

The SBOM of the same subject, as a BOM-Link with a hash. It is how a consumer reaches components the CBOM does not describe, and how a library named under I9 is placed in the dependency tree.

Where the producer publishes statements about whether this subject is affected by a vulnerability (VEX, CSAF VEX, or an exploitability statement). Either a fixed document, with a hash, or a feed or API, with its access protocol named. A producer that publishes none says so ('not-published'). Silence

Where third-party or vendor advisories about the subject and its libraries are published, with the access protocol named: a web page, a CSAF provider, the OSV API or the GitHub advisory API. A machine-readable endpoint lets a consumer query by the package URLs the CBOM already carries.
Where to report a weakness or request a fuller disclosure. The objective lists 'request a fuller disclosure from the producer' as a decision option; without a contact, that option has no address.

If a product states that the operator decides an algorithm, the interface points to where the operator decides it. 'deployment-defined' without this pointer tells the operator that the decision is theirs and not how to make it.
A threat model or design document. This is where design intention is recorded now that 'intended' is not an accepted stage: as context the record points to, not as a stage it reports.
